correctness.rationale: For every full-dimensional convex K in \(d\ge2\), the covariogram g has \(g(0)=\operatorname{vol}(K)\), vanishes at the difference-body boundary, and is \(1/d\)-root-concave by a Brunn–Minkowski overlap inclusion. Thus on each normalized radial ray the likelihood-ratio \(w(r)=g(rR(\theta)\theta)/(\operatorname{vol}(K)(1-r)^d)\) is nondecreasing. Polar disintegration makes the conditional gauge radius a monotone-likelihood-ratio tilt of \(\mathrm{Beta}(d,d+1)\), giving every CDF inequality. Nonconstant tilts give strictness for every interior t; equality implies \(g(z)=\operatorname{vol}(K)(1-\gamma_D(z))^d\), and integration yields equality in Rogers–Shephard, characterizing simplices. Barycentric overlap geometry proves all simplices attain the beta law. All moment constants and boundary cases have been algebraically checked. Supplementary exact tests/Monte Carlo run from the packaged verify.py; finite checks are not offered as proof.

Its implication from known concavity is explicit, not denied; this nontrivial distributional consequence and its strict equality case are the asserted mathematical gap.

originality.rationale: Originality is attributed only to the sharp, all-threshold first-order stochastic bound for the intrinsic difference-body gauge of a random point pair, together with simplex-only equality. The underlying covariogram root-concavity (Langharst 2022 Proposition 2.5), simplex rigidity (Proposition 2.6), radial mean body framework (Gardner–Zhang 1998), and Rogers–Shephard volume inequality are known and cited. The inspected full primary papers concern inverse covariograms, radial-moment inclusions, or Zhang-type measure comparisons, not the same normalized gauge CDF. A corresponding general measure or older stochastic formulation remains a genuine historical risk because the 1998 original full text was unavailable.
residual_risks: The full text of Gardner–Zhang (1998) was not obtained; an older equivalent likelihood-ratio or normalized gauge probability formulation remains a priority risk.

A general stochastic order for concave profiles in older probability literature could imply the theorem after a nontrivial covariogram-to-gauge specialization; the searches are not a novelty certificate.
The 2022 published root-concavity statement is a substantial premise of the proof; the present contribution claims the explicit conditional stochastic-order deduction, not novelty of that premise.

value.rationale: For a natural, affine-invariant random-pair geometric statistic the theorem determines a sharp dimension-only stochastic benchmark at every quantile, a unique extremizing class, and sharp bounds for the entire continuum of positive power moments. It is not a selective scalar moment or arbitrary numerical slice. Motivating prior work considers covariograms, radial mean bodies, and Rogers–Shephard asymmetry; the new direction is an explicit probability law converting ray-wise root-concavity to universal conditional likelihood-ratio domination. The exact planar-square gap demonstrates genuinely strict behavior outside simplices. Historical overlap caveats are separately disclosed.
